question: At what degree from the epicentre does the seismograph record the arrival of P-waves but NOT S-waves?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Beyond 145º**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Seismographs record the arrival of P-waves but not S-waves at angles beyond 145º from the earthquake's epicenter.
 
• This is due to the presence of the Earth's liquid outer core, which S-waves cannot travel through.
 
• P-waves, or primary waves, are compressional waves that can travel through both solid and liquid layers of the Earth.
 
• S-waves, or secondary waves, are shear waves and can only travel through solid materials.
 
• The shadow zone for S-waves is created because they are blocked by the liquid outer core.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Seismology:**

 
 
• Seismology is the scientific study of earthquakes and the propagation of elastic waves through the Earth.
 
• It plays a crucial role in understanding the Earth's internal structure and dynamics.
 
 
 
• **Epicenter and Focus:**
 
 
• The epicenter is the point on the Earth's surface directly above the focus, where an earthquake originates.
 
• The focus is the location within the Earth where the earthquake rupture starts.
 
 
 
• **Types of Seismic Waves:**
 
 
• P-waves (Primary waves): Compressional waves that travel fastest through the Earth.
 
• S-waves (Secondary waves): Shear waves that travel slower than P-waves and cannot pass through liquids.
 
• Surface waves: Travel along the Earth's surface and generally cause the most damage during an earthquake.
 
 
 
• **Seismic Shadow Zones:**
 
 
• The area of the Earth that does not receive any direct P-waves is called the P-wave shadow zone, typically found between 104º and 140º from the earthquake's epicenter.
 
• The S-wave shadow zone extends from 104º to 180º, as S-waves are completely blocked by the liquid outer core.
